vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: meituan-c-user-auth
Version: 1.0.7

The skill bundle is a legitimate authentication utility for Meituan C-end users, designed to handle SMS login and token management. It follows security best practices by implementing strict file permissions (0600) for local token storage via a dedicated cache manager (skill_cache_cli.py) and communicates exclusively with official Meituan endpoints (peppermall.meituan.com). The logic for version checking via clawhub.ai and the platform-specific cron job configurations for automated coupon collection are transparently documented and align with the tool's stated purpose without evidence of malicious intent or data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill implements Meituan SMS-login and token management as described, but it also scans and migrates token files from other locations (including OpenClaw/default workspaces), claims an official affiliation without provenance, and centralizes tokens — behaviors that exceed what's clearly necessary and warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to provide SMS-based Meituan user authentication and manage a user_token/device_token, which matches the included scripts. However the package also claims an official Meituan authorship in the runtime instructions while the registry metadata has no homepage/source provenance — a misleading claim. Additionally, the code explicitly looks for and/or migrates token files from multiple legacy paths (including ~/.openclaw/workspace/auth_tokens.json and other agent workspaces). Reading and consolidating tokens from other skills/workspaces is beyond a minimal "authentication helper" and is disproportionate unless the user explicitly consents to migration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to execute bundled Python scripts, perform remote version checks via clawhub.ai, open the system browser for terms, contact Meituan endpoints, and enforce timezone adjustments. More importantly, the instructions and auth.py's logic perform local filesystem discovery and migration of existing auth/token files from multiple locations (legacy paths and detected workspaces). That behavior reads sensitive data belonging to other skills or contexts and is not limited to the skill's own storage.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install spec (instruction-only + bundled Python scripts). No remote downloads or package installs are performed by the skill itself, which reduces supply-chain risk. However the bundled scripts will be executed locally and perform filesystem and network operations, so the absence of a download step does not eliminate runtime risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but the code reads and honors many optional environment variables (SKILL_CACHE_CLI_PATH, SKILL_CACHE_PYTHON, SKILL_CACHE_WORKSPACE, CLAUDE_WORKSPACE, XIAOMEI_WORKSPACE, XIAOMEI_AUTH_FILE). It will probe default locations (e.g. ~/.xiaomei-workspace, ~/.openclaw/workspace) and migrate found tokens into a shared cache. Requesting or accessing those locations and environment variables is broad relative to a simple SMS-login helper and can expose tokens from other skills.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists tokens and terms_accepted state to a shared cache file (.shared/mt_auth_tokens.json) and will migrate legacy auth files into that central location. Centralizing tokens increases the blast radius (multiple skills may read from the shared cache). The skill does not request 'always: true', but the migration and workspace-detection behaviors effectively allow it to access and re-persist credentials from other contexts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill largely does what it claims (send SMS, verify code, store tokens), but it also searches for and migrates existing auth/token files from other agent workspaces (including an OpenClaw path) and instructs the agent to present text claiming official Meituan authorship despite no provenance. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the publisher/source (ask for official repo/homepage or vendor attestation). 2) If you decide to run it, run in an isolated environment (sandbox or throwaway account) to avoid accidental token consolidation. 3) Set XIAOMEI_AUTH_FILE or SKILL_CACHE_WORKSPACE to a dedicated path (e.g., /tmp/mt-auth.json) to force storage into an isolated file and prevent automatic migration. 4) Backup any existing auth files (e.g., ~/.openclaw/workspace/auth_tokens.json, ~/.xiaomei-workspace/*.json) before first run. 5) Inspect/modify the migration functions in scripts/auth.py to remove unwanted legacy-path scanning if you want to keep tokens separate. 6) Confirm network endpoints (https://peppermall.meituan.com and clawhub.ai) are expected for your use and that you have legal authorization to use those APIs. If you cannot verify the author or are uncomfortable with automatic migration/centralization of tokens, do not install or run this skill.
